plan: My private value is $13. In a second-price sealed bid auction, optimal strategy is to bid close to my true value. I want to win if possible, but not overpay. Since values are randomly drawn, I'll bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances, but not so high that I risk negative profit. A bid around $14-$15 seems strategic - high enough to likely win, but not excessively risky.

My private value is $11. In a first-price sealed bid auction, I want to bid strategically to maximize potential profit. Since values are randomly drawn, I'll aim to bid slightly below my true value to create a buffer. A bid around $9-$10 allows me potential profit if I win, while protecting against overbidding. This strategy balances the risk of losing the auction with the risk of winning but paying too much relative to my value.

My private value is $12. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This prevents underbidding (and potentially losing a profitable item) or overbidding (and reducing potential profit). Since values are independently drawn, I can't predict others' values precisely. Bidding $12 ensures I win if my value is highest, and I'll only pay the second-highest bid, maximizing my potential profit.
